meta.title: Register-data claims
meta.tagline: What an empirical paper says it found (abstract, refined by the introduction), as atomic directional claims, each traced to the table result that shows it.
meta.description: One entry per stated claim: cause, effect, sign and scope, the abstract sentence that anchors it, the introduction sentence that says how the finding was obtained, and the table (or figure) results that operationalise it with their point estimates. Written for economics papers using Danish register data (the danish-register-econ protocol), usable for any empirical paper. Pair it with the Register-data tables preset: a companion tables dataset lets Metalens cross-check every point estimate against the independently transcribed table cell. The records are produced OUTSIDE Metalens by the danish-register-econ agent pipeline, which reads each paper in several passes; this preset is the schema they are imported into, not the recipe that made them.

fields.name: abstract_source
fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: printed = the PDF carries the paper's abstract (usually on its first page); none = no abstract is printed, in which case claims must be empty

entries.label: Stated claim
entries.help: one atomic, directional finding the ABSTRACT states or announces (refined by the introduction where the abstract only announces it); comparisons and not_causal statements are listed too so nothing is silently dropped
entries.title: {claim_id} · {statement}

fields.name: claim_id
fields.label: Claim id
fields.help: S1, S2, … in the order of the abstract

fields.name: type
fields.label: Type
fields.help: edge = a causal effect of one variable on another; comparison = the abstract compares effects (larger for A than B) and qualifies edges; not_causal = a descriptive fact, method or data presented as a finding

fields.name: statement
fields.label: Statement
fields.help: '<cause> increases | decreases | has no effect on | has mixed effects on <effect>' — no numbers, no 'significantly', no method, setting or population; for not_causal the sentence's finding in one line

fields.name: cause
fields.label: Cause
fields.help: the cause as the abstract names it: a short noun phrase, no transformation ('earnings', not 'log earnings'); null for not_causal

fields.name: effect
fields.label: Effect
fields.help: the effect as the abstract names it; null for not_causal

fields.name: cause_construct
fields.label: Cause construct
fields.help: the broader construct the cause is an indicator of, when this paper measures one construct through several variables: 'tax incentives' for 'marginal net-of-tax rate'. Write it the SAME way in every claim that indicates it; null when the cause IS the construct

fields.name: effect_construct
fields.label: Effect construct
fields.help: the broader construct the effect is an indicator of: 'mental health' for 'use of psychological assistance', 'prescriptions for mental-health conditions' and 'opioid prescriptions' — three claims, one construct, written identically in all three. Null when the effect IS the construct

fields.name: construct_basis
fields.label: Construct basis
fields.help: stated = the paper itself presents these variables as measuring the construct ('we study mental health, measured by …'); inferred = treating them as indicators of one construct is YOUR reading. Null when no construct is named

fields.name: construct_note
fields.label: Construct assumption
fields.help: the auxiliary assumption in one sentence — 'opioid prescriptions are treated as an indicator of mental health'. It is what a reviewer judges; write it whenever the basis is inferred

fields.name: sign
fields.label: Sign
fields.help: in the paper's own orientation: + increases, - decreases, 0 the authors report testing and finding no effect, mixed the sign differs across groups or settings and the text says so; null for not_causal

fields.name: anchor_quote
fields.label: Abstract anchor
fields.help: the abstract sentence that states or announces this finding, VERBATIM (at most 60 words); cite it with source 'abstract'

fields.name: intro_sentence
fields.label: Introduction sentence
fields.help: the introduction sentence that completes the claim (which variables, which direction) or says HOW the finding was obtained — the design, the sample, the comparison, the exhibit; VERBATIM, at most 60 words, source 'introduction'; null when the abstract alone carries everything and the introduction adds nothing

fields.name: support
fields.label: Support
fields.help: explicit = the anchor alone states cause, effect and direction; assembled = anchor plus introduction sentence(s) together state all three; weak = a variable or the direction is your inference (say which in notes). Never upgraded

fields.name: refined_by_introduction
fields.label: Refined by the introduction
fields.help: true when the abstract only announces the finding and the introduction supplied the variables or the direction

fields.name: scope_setting
fields.label: Setting
fields.help: where: 'Denmark, administrative registers'; null when not stated

fields.name: scope_period
fields.label: Period
fields.help: when: '1980 to 2019'; null when not stated

fields.name: scope_population
fields.label: Population
fields.help: who the finding is about: 'wage earners', 'men'. A finding that differs only in who it is about is a separate claim with the same cause and effect; null when not stated

fields.name: scope_identification
fields.label: Identification
fields.help: how the effect is identified, in the authors' words: 'matched-control difference-in-differences exploiting the timing of sudden parental deaths'; null when not stated

fields.name: magnitude_stated
fields.label: Stated magnitude
fields.help: a magnitude the abstract or introduction states, verbatim ('earnings decline by 2 percent'); null when none is stated

fields.name: qualifies
fields.label: Qualifies
fields.help: comparison claims only: the claim ids of the edges compared

fields.name: moderator
fields.label: Moderator
fields.help: comparison claims only: what the effect is compared across ('gender', 'firm size')

fields.name: relation
fields.label: Relation
fields.help: comparison claims only: the comparison stated ('larger for women than for men')

fields.name: notes
fields.label: Notes
fields.help: what a reader must know: which variable or direction was inferred (weak support), why no result matches ('shown only graphically'), flags

children.label: Table result
children.help: the extracted results that OPERATIONALISE the claim: a table column (or a figure) whose target regressor measures the cause, whose outcome measures the effect, and whose setting, period, population and design fall inside the claim's scope. Prefer few, right matches over many plausible ones; at most two 'main' per claim unless the finding is genuinely carried by several estimates. Empty when nothing matches — do not force a match
children.title: {source_table} {panel} {column}

fields.name: result_id
fields.label: Result id
fields.help: R1, R2, … within the claim

fields.name: estimand
fields.label: Estimand
fields.help: a short key for WHAT is estimated, identical for every estimate of the same quantity and different whenever the quantity differs: '<claim>/<subgroup>/<horizon>' ('S1/men/years-0-1', 'S3/all/5y', 'S2/all/discrete-exposure'). Exactly ONE estimate per estimand is the preferred one (role main); the others are the same quantity measured again

fields.name: role
fields.label: Role
fields.help: main = the estimate the authors would point to for this finding; supporting = another specification of the same finding they rely on; robustness; heterogeneity = a subgroup split of it

fields.name: exhibit
fields.label: Exhibit
fields.help: which exhibit shows the ANALYSIS this estimate comes from — a table, a figure, or none when the paper reports the analysis only in prose ('in unreported regressions …'). Fill it even when the number itself is not printed there: the exhibit is what tells a reader the estimator, the sample and the specification

fields.name: source_table
fields.label: Table / figure
fields.help: the exhibit as printed: 'Table 3', 'Table A2', 'Figure 4' — the analysis this estimate belongs to, even when its value is only stated in the text; null only when the paper shows no exhibit for it

fields.name: panel
fields.label: Panel
fields.help: the panel label ('A', 'B') or null when the table has no panels

fields.name: column
fields.label: Column
fields.help: the column label exactly as printed: '(2)', 'Percent'; null for a figure

fields.name: row_label
fields.label: Row
fields.help: the row label of the coefficient as printed; for a figure the annotation or series it comes from

fields.name: subgroup
fields.label: Subgroup
fields.help: who this estimate is for when the column or panel restricts the claim's population: 'men', 'women', 'top earnings quartile', 'manufacturing'. Null when it covers the claim's whole population. The claim itself stays general — the subgroup lives here, so the estimates for men and women stay apart

fields.name: horizon
fields.label: Horizon
fields.help: the window this estimate covers when the paper reports several: 'years 0-1', 'year 5', 'the post-reform period', 'long run'. Null when the paper reports only one. As printed in the panel or column heading

fields.name: outcome_variable
fields.label: Outcome
fields.help: the dependent variable of that column as the paper names it

fields.name: regressor
fields.label: Regressor
fields.help: the coefficient's regressor as printed (the treatment, the instrumented variable, the policy variable)

fields.name: value_from
fields.label: Number from
fields.help: where the NUMBER comes from: printed = it is printed in the exhibit (a table cell, a figure annotation); text = the exhibit does not print it but the paper states it in prose ('women visit psychologists 0.10 more times per year'); absent = the paper reports no number for this estimate. Only a printed table value can be cross-checked against the transcribed cells

fields.name: point_estimate
fields.label: Point estimate
fields.help: the coefficient exactly as printed in that cell (sign, every digit; stars, parentheses and commas stripped); for a figure only a value the figure PRINTS (an annotation) — never read off an axis; null when no number is printed

fields.name: estimate_se
fields.label: Standard error
fields.help: the standard error printed for that coefficient (the parenthesised value); null when the table prints a t-statistic or p-value instead, or nothing

fields.name: treatment_relation
fields.label: Treatment relation
fields.help: direct = the regressor measures the cause itself; proxy; assignment = a treatment-group, reform or instrument indicator standing in for the cause

fields.name: outcome_relation
fields.label: Outcome relation
fields.help: direct = the outcome measures the effect itself; proxy

fields.name: sign_consistent
fields.label: Sign consistent
fields.help: read in its OWN variable orientation, does the estimate agree with the claim's direction? (a net-of-tax-rate elasticity of +0.2 agrees with 'the tax rate decreases income'); null when there is no estimate or it cannot be told. A disagreeing result is still a match — that is a finding

fields.name: why
fields.label: Why
fields.help: one sentence: why this result operationalises the claim (and, for a comparison, which side it is)

groups.label: Claim
groups.help: type, statement, sign, support: is this what the abstract states?

groups.label: Results
groups.help: the right table cell, the right role, the value as printed

default_dashboard.title: Point estimates by paper
default_dashboard.main_message: One dot per matched table result, as printed; scales differ across papers.
